question.text:
The actual CPU bursts of a process begin as: $$6, 4, 6, 4, 13, \ldots$$

The initial predicted CPU burst is: $\tau_0 = 10$ 

Using exponential averaging with: 

$$\alpha = 0.7$$

What is the predicted CPU burst length after incorporating the first three actual CPU bursts? 

Use: $$\tau_{n+1} = \alpha t_n + (1-\alpha)\tau_n$$ (Round the answer to two decimal places.)
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider the following processes: 

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Job} & \text{Arrival Time} & \text{CPU Burst Time} \\ \hline A & 0 & 8 \\ B & 2 & 4 \\ C & 5 & 7 \\ \hline \end{array} $$

Given an FCFS scheduler, what is the average turnaround time of the three jobs? 

  1. $10$ seconds 
     
  2. $10\frac{1}{3}$ seconds 
     
  3. $10\frac{2}{3}$ seconds 
     
  4. $13$ seconds
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Three jobs arrive at approximately the same time, with $A$ arriving slightly before $B$, and $B$ slightly before $C$. 

Their CPU burst times are: $A = 2$ seconds $B = 8$ seconds $C = 7$ seconds 

Given an SJF scheduler, what is the average response time of the three jobs? 

  1. $2$ seconds 
     
  2. $3.67$ seconds 
     
  3. $9$ seconds 
     
  4. $9.33$ seconds

question.text:

  1. Waiting time
     
  2. Response time
     
  3. Throughput
     
  4. Page-fault rate

question.text:
Which of the following statements are correct? 

  1. A FIFO scheduler has lower average turnaround time when long jobs arrive after short jobs, compared with when short jobs arrive after long jobs. 
     
  2. An SJF scheduler may preempt the currently running job. 
     
  3. An SJF scheduler can suffer from the convoy effect. 
     
  4. If all jobs arrive at the same point in time, SJF and Shortest-Time-to-Completion-First behave the same.
